sections.overview: British records place this tortricid mainly in England and Wales. The Belgian catalogue describes it as widespread but rare in that country.
sections.identification: Adults have a white forewing pattern with chestnut and grey markings and a wingspan of about 19–24 mm.
sections.habitat: British accounts record it in woodland, gardens, orchards, parks and marshes.
sections.diet: The larvae feed inside spun leaves or shoots of sallows and poplars.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in summer and may be attracted to light.
sections.reproduction: The larvae tie leaves or shoots together with silk; the consulted summaries do not detail egg laying.
sections.ecology: Its documented larval hosts are woody Salix and Populus, and the caterpillar lives concealed within the spun foliage.
sections.conservation: The regional sources describe occurrence and host plants but do not give a global threat category.
